site.bio:
i write narratives for companies doing extreme things, so the rest of the world gets it.
because the future usually sounds scary before it sounds useful and my job is to close that gap

kalshi (nda), retell ai, deel, bitgo, ricursive intelligence, evolving ai & greg isenberg.

posts.title: who's she??
posts.body:
I easily spend eight hours a day on X, but my real edge isn't just keeping up with internet speed..it's going one level deeper to interpret what actually matters.

I live at the intersection of fast-moving tech and deep human psychology. When I'm not into the timeline, I’m reading books like The Rational Optimist, Sex at Dawn, or Shoe Dog, or geeking out over Freud and Carl Jung.

I’m a high-agency person who loves the scrappy side of building. I’ve been a PM, designer, writer, consultant, and recruiter..often all at once and I live by one rule: a day doesn't count unless I’ve created something tangible. 
Haven't missed a day yet 😉

Right now, AI is stuck between wild tech breakthroughs and public doomsday panic. I bridge that gap, using psychology and storytelling to translate complex tech into narratives normal people actually care about.

posts.title: deel: launch
posts.body:
Akai: customer testimonial video

- Creative directed Akai's testimonial video end to end.
- Chose which customers to feature, picking voices that would make the product's   value land with the right audience.
- Gave each one a shooting brief covering framing, setup and delivery, so footage recorded in different places would cut together as one piece.
- Guided what each person spoke about, shaping the talking points in advance so every clip carried a piece of the story.
- Collected the raw files and handled the full post production: selected the strongest moments, built the narrative edit, and chose the music and on screen design.

[akai testimonial](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/akai-run_the-workflows-that-keep-a-business-running-activity-7473177673561788416-V8Jm?utm_source=social_share_send&utm_medium=member_desktop_web&rcm=ACoAADa76iwBUSmZcnzUjLb3z07oj4InktE8aG8)

posts.title: Lightspeed Venture Partners
posts.body:
Podcast narrative edit

Took a raw, unscripted podcast of almost two hours and turned it into a tight, story-led cut.
Reviewed the full footage, chose the strongest moments and built the narrative arc around them.
Owned every editorial call: what stayed, what went, and how it was sequenced.

Investor and hiring motion video

Owned the project end to end, from brief to final cut.
Learned the product in depth to turn complex technology into a story anyone could follow.
Developed the angle, wrote the hook and the script, and directed the motion design.
The video was circulated to investors for the company's next funding round and used to attract new hires.

posts.title: retell ai: launch narrative
posts.body:
Started from a one-line brief: make a launch video that feels bigger than life. No script, no reference, no defined story.
Translated that brief into a clear strategic angle: what the launch needed to make people feel, and why it mattered beyond the feature set.
Turned the angle into a rough draft, then sharpened it into the final script, building the hook and the arc so the scale came from the story itself.
Storyboarded the script shot by shot to lock the pacing, visual language and key moments before production started.
Led creative direction end to end, guiding the edit and visuals until the finished video delivered on "bigger than life"

[check here](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/retellai_there-was-a-time-when-a-conversation-meant-activity-7440099093605130240-O966?utm_source=social_share_send&utm_medium=member_desktop_web&rcm=ACoAADa76iwBUSmZcnzUjLb3z07oj4InktE8aG8)

posts.title: hiring
posts.body:
i have a thing for spotting people. four writers on our team came through me, all found in the wild: twitter threads, reddit discussions, communities, rooms i walked into. no job posts, no forms. i'd rather read how someone thinks than read their cv.

i believe: the best people aren't applying. they're busy being good somewhere else
